    <cbc:Name languageID="ENG">Competence brokers for research mobilisation in Troms.</cbc:Name>
    
    <cbc:Description languageID="ENG">Background

Troms County, c/o the FORREGION Troms section development and innovation, needs external assistance with research mobilisation in business. The aim is to strengthen the link between companies and relevant research and development environments and contribute to having several entities in Troms initiate research and innovation projects.

FORREGION is responsible for research based innovation in the regions and is a subsidy scheme aimed at companies with little or no experience with research and development work. The procurement shall support the scheme's aim of increasing the share of R&D in business through mobilisation, closer connection between businesses and R&D environments and that preliminary projects to a greater degree lead on to main projects and other continued research activity.

The procurement will be implemented as the county needs capacity and expertise to work systematically, outreach and needs managed towards companies, particularly small and medium sized entities who have little experience with research and development. At the same time, there is a need to make relevant R&D environments, financing schemes and other means more accessible for businesses in the region.

The assignment shall support the aim of increased research efforts in business, several qualified applications for relevant research resources and better regional coverage in the mobilisation work. It is particularly important to mobilise research-independent companies in prioritised branches, facilitate more lasting co-operation relationships between businesses and R&D actors and contribute to the continuation of promising initiatives from early idea phases and preliminary projects to major development and research projects.

Description of the assignment

The contracting authority shall procure assistance from a total of five competence broker teams for research mobilisation in Troms. The resources shall collectively cover the topic areas seafood, space activity/space, KI and technology development as well as Circular Troms, where two of the sub-contracts shall be related to seafood. Each sub-contract shall be taken care of by a competence broker team with relevant and complementary competence within the relevant input area.

The target group for the assignment is small and medium sized companies that belong to Troms county, or who have considerable activity in Troms. Competence brokering shall be a free offer to the target group. The assignment requires that the competence brokers act independently and neutrally and that they do not represent business actors who can be in a competitive relationship with the companies that receive assistance. The competence brokers shall sign a confidentiality statement.

The delivery includes outreach contact with companies, needs analysis, mapping of relevant R&D partners, connection between companies and research environments as well as guidance in the development of R&D projects and applications for research resources. Follow-up shall be adapted to each company's need and maturity, and can include assistance from early idea clarification and preliminary project for further mobilisation with main projects and other relevant schemes. The competence broker shall be a consultant and supervisor in application processes, but shall not write applications on behalf of the companies or act in competition with private actors.

The competence broker teams shall be able to identify the companies ́ need for research and innovation, contribute to finding relevant research competence and guide the companies towards appropriate sources of financing. This includes FORREGION and other relevant schemes, e.g. Tax Finds, The Research Council of Norway, Innovation Norway, Horizon Europe and other relevant means. Where it is natural, the competence brokers should also refer to other actors in the funding apparatus.

The assignment includes further follow-up of companies that have previously carried out preliminary projects financed by FORREGION Troms, with the aim of contributing to further development and execution of main projects. The competence brokers shall also be able to arrange network meetings between businesses and R&D actors in order to identify common problems, possibilities for research and development, as well as strengthen the sharing of knowledge and cooperation.

Resources are requested with relevant experience from research mobilisation in business, a good understanding of regional innovation and R&D environments, knowledge of relevant businesses in the region and the ability to work needs controlled. The role requires good collaboration abilities, good communication comprehension and the ability to build trust in both companies and research environments. The competence brokers shall furthermore cooperate with other competence brokers in FORREGION, other innovation actors in Troms and participate in relevant regional and national gatherings, including obligatory training and gathering activities managed by the Research Council of Norway.

The assignment also includes reporting to the contracting authority through fixed digital reporting systems and templates. The reporting shall, among other things, provide an overview of completed mediations, resource use, contact with R&D institutions, projects that are brokered on to relevant schemes, preliminary projects, network meetings and other relevant results and activities.</cbc:Description>

normalized.title: Competence brokers for research mobilisation in Troms.
normalized.description:
Background

Troms County, c/o the FORREGION Troms section development and innovation, needs external assistance with research mobilisation in business. The aim is to strengthen the link between companies and relevant research and development environments and contribute to having several entities in Troms initiate research and innovation projects.

FORREGION is responsible for research based innovation in the regions and is a subsidy scheme aimed at companies with little or no experience with research and development work. The procurement shall support the scheme's aim of increasing the share of R&D in business through mobilisation, closer connection between businesses and R&D environments and that preliminary projects to a greater degree lead on to main projects and other continued research activity.

The procurement will be implemented as the county needs capacity and expertise to work systematically, outreach and needs managed towards companies, particularly small and medium sized entities who have little experience with research and development. At the same time, there is a need to make relevant R&D environments, financing schemes and other means more accessible for businesses in the region.

The assignment shall support the aim of increased research efforts in business, several qualified applications for relevant research resources and better regional coverage in the mobilisation work. It is particularly important to mobilise research-independent companies in prioritised branches, facilitate more lasting co-operation relationships between businesses and R&D actors and contribute to the continuation of promising initiatives from early idea phases and preliminary projects to major development and research projects.

Description of the assignment

The contracting authority shall procure assistance from a total of five competence broker teams for research mobilisation in Troms. The resources shall collectively cover the topic areas seafood, space activity/space, KI and technology development as well as Circular Troms, where two of the sub-contracts shall be related to seafood. Each sub-contract shall be taken care of by a competence broker team with relevant and complementary competence within the relevant input area.

The target group for the assignment is small and medium sized companies that belong to Troms county, or who have considerable activity in Troms. Competence brokering shall be a free offer to the target group. The assignment requires that the competence brokers act independently and neutrally and that they do not represent business actors who can be in a competitive relationship with the companies that receive assistance. The competence brokers shall sign a confidentiality statement.

The delivery includes outreach contact with companies, needs analysis, mapping of relevant R&D partners, connection between companies and research environments as well as guidance in the development of R&D projects and applications for research resources. Follow-up shall be adapted to each company's need and maturity, and can include assistance from early idea clarification and preliminary project for further mobilisation with main projects and other relevant schemes. The competence broker shall be a consultant and supervisor in application processes, but shall not write applications on behalf of the companies or act in competition with private actors.

The competence broker teams shall be able to identify the companies ́ need for research and innovation, contribute to finding relevant research competence and guide the companies towards appropriate sources of financing. This includes FORREGION and other relevant schemes, e.g. Tax Finds, The Research Council of Norway, Innovation Norway, Horizon Europe and other relevant means. Where it is natural, the competence brokers should also refer to other actors in the funding apparatus.

The assignment includes further follow-up of companies that have previously carried out preliminary projects financed by FORREGION Troms, with the aim of contributing to further development and execution of main projects. The competence brokers shall also be able to arrange network meetings between businesses and R&D actors in order to identify common problems, possibilities for research and development, as well as strengthen the sharing of knowledge and cooperation.

Resources are requested with relevant experience from research mobilisation in business, a good understanding of regional innovation and R&D environments, knowledge of relevant businesses in the region and the ability to work needs controlled. The role requires good collaboration abilities, good communication comprehension and the ability to build trust in both companies and research environments. The competence brokers shall furthermore cooperate with other competence brokers in FORREGION, other innovation actors in Troms and participate in relevant regional and national gatherings, including obligatory training and gathering activities managed by the Research Council of Norway.

The assignment also includes reporting to the contracting authority through fixed digital reporting systems and templates. The reporting shall, among other things, provide an overview of completed mediations, resource use, contact with R&D institutions, projects that are brokered on to relevant schemes, preliminary projects, network meetings and other relevant results and activities.

normalized.title: S2-SW-10: CANADIAN PARTICIPATION IN THE ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK FEASIBILITY STUDY
normalized.description: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.

normalized.title: HIGHLY-INTEGRATED AND EFFICIENT MILLIMETRE-WAVE PHASED ARRAY ANTENNA USING ADVANCED PACKAGING SOLUTION (ARTES AT 5B.258) - RE-ISSUE
normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test a highly integrated and efficient millimetre-wave phased array antenna using advanced packaging solution for multi-chip,multi-technology assembly, including 3-dimensional heterogeneous integration interconnects, thermal and power management.Targeted Improvements:Enabling disruptive technology to enable thermal management of highly integrated phased arrays, with a twice the RF power handling capability.Description: The development and deployment of millimetre-wave phased array antennas present several challenges that can reduce their efficiency and performance. These challenges include low RF power per element across different orbits (Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), and Geostationary EarthOrbit (GEO)) due to the use of silicon chips and the inefficiency in thermal management. Further limitations are introduced by the use of 2D packaging, which prevents the integration of high-power handling capabilities and enhanced thermal management technologies.The power efficiency and dependability of the antenna are reduced by signal strength degradation caused by the low RF output power per element. These performance issues directly affect satellite-to-ground communication as well as intersatellite communication.Toovercome these limitations, transitioning from 2D to 3D Heterogeneous Integration (3DHI) interconnect technology can significantly improve the thermal and power performance of phased array antennas. By stacking components vertically, more space can be allocated for effective thermal management, and the integration of multiple layers with thermal vias allows for better heat dissipation. This approach also enables the integration of diverse materials and technologies within the same package. Novel materials like Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) offer superior thermal conductivity and higher power handling capabilities compared to traditional silicon. Incorporating thesematerials into the antenna array, using an Integrated Antenna-on-Chip (AoC) approach, can increase the RF power per element while alleviating thermal constraints.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 will develop an antenna concept, investigate and develop key processes necessary to fabricate a millimetre-wave 3DHI active antenna.This includes integrating low-power silicon chips, RF power amplifiers, thermal management solutions and advanced packaging techniques. During this phase, critical components will be developed to breadboard level to assess the effectiveness of 3D packaging methods, such as vertical integration and thermal vias, in addressing thermal dissipation and RF power handling challenges. Phase 1 outputwill deliver an antenna concept supported by critical breadboard test results. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 1,000 kEuro.- Phase2 will focus on developing a scaled engineering model of a millimetre-wave phased array antenna using 3DHI technology in Q, V, orW-Bands. Phase 2 will include refining the design, manufacturing, and testing the antenna's performance in representative operational environments.

normalized.title: ESTRACK BACK-END CONTRACTS
normalized.description: A new approach to engineering, sustaining and third-level maintenance is proposed for the Back-End installations at the Deep Spacesites in New Norcia, Cebreros, and Malarge, the Near-Earth sites in Kiruna and Kourou, and the Ground Station Reference Facility(GSRF) at ESOC. Under this approach, following a successful phase-in, the end-to-end responsibility for these installations shall betaken over by the prime contractor. The term Back-End refers in the ESTRACK terminology to the systems integrating the Tracking,Telemetry, Command Processor, the ground systems test and validation infrastructure, Frequency and Timing subsystem and the IT infrastructure of the ground stations. The contractual scope of this procurement proposal includes integration and sustaining activities, predictive and corrective maintenance of the various backend subsystems and subsystem retests, spares and repair procurement and third-level support to the Maintenance and Operations (MO) teams for all ESTRACK terminals.

Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. normalized.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time.
